answer: Coordination Prism Pricing. Each agent action must reference a distinct recent co-action partner, forming a directed graph; identities whose partners overlap heavily get their shared coordination surface re-priced upward, like light splitting through a prism. The fee scales with local clustering, so a sybil ring pays a glacier of accumulating costs as its members keep re-coordinating. Honest sparse pairs stay on a flat mesa of low fees. Attacker cost: each fake identity needs genuinely distinct counterparties, making N sybils cost N times the marginal coordination fee.
